question: Sudhir claimed to sell his items at only 8% above the cost of production, but used a weight that had 750 grams written on it, though it actually weighed 720 grams. What was the actual profit percentage earned by Sudhir?
solution:
**FORMULA USED:**

Profit = S.P. - C.P.

Profit% = (Profit/C.P.) × 100

Where, S.P = Selling price, C.P. = Cost price 

**CALCULATION:**

Sudhir sells his items at an 8% profit 

⇒ Profit% =( Profit /C.P.) × 100

⇒ 8 = (S.P. - C.P.)/C.P. × 100 

⇒ 108 C.P. = 100 S.P. or S.P.= 1.08 C.P.

But when Sudhir uses weights that measure only 720 grams while he claims to measure 750 grams

Hence, C.P. of 720 grams = (720/750) × Original C.P. = 0.96 of original C.P.

So, he is selling goods worth 0.96 at 1.08 C.P. 

⇒ Hence, he makes a profit of ( 1.08 - 0.96) = 0.12 C.P. on his cost of 0.96 C.P.

⇒ Profit% = ( 0.12/ 0.96) × 100 = 12.5

**Hence, actual Profit percentage earned by Sudhir is 12.5%.**
